log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Incineroar leads well with Intimidate and Fake Out to blunt physical attackers like Garchomp and Kingambit. Garchomp gives fast physical pressure, and Gholdengo adds strong special coverage to threaten the bulky Steel and Grass types.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Since the opponent's team mirrors ours, I'm thinking about which three to bring and lead with. Incineroar feels like a strong lead with Fake Out and Intimidate support, paired with Garchomp for speed and power and Kingambit as another hard hitter, while weighing how to handle their own Garchomp.

I'll go with Incineroar, Garchomp, and Gholdengo for coverage, leading with Incineroar.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is slower than Garchomp, so Fake Out is the only way to act first. Its +3 priority and flinch stop Garchomp from attacking this turn. Flare Blitz is resisted by Dragon.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: It's turn one, my Incineroar against a full-health Garchomp that's already taken an attack drop. Fake Out seems like the obvious play here since it gets priority, guarantees a flinch, and chips some damage regardless of Garchomp's likely speed advantage.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is slower than the mega Garchomp, and Flare Blitz is resisted by its Dragon typing. Parting Shot drops Garchomp's Attack to -2 and its Special Attack to -1, weakening its physical hits. It also pivots Incineroar out before Earthquake or Outrage can hit it for super-effective damage.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking matchup details: the opposing Mega Garchomp is at 88% HP with its attack lowered from intimidate, and it outspeeds my Incineroar. Flare Blitz would only be half-effective against its Dragon/Ground typing, so I need to weigh whether Incineroar's fire attack is even worth using here given the resistance.

I'm weighing whether to Protect and stall, or Parting Shot to debuff Garchomp while switching to Gholdengo -- though Gholdengo's Steel and Shadow Ball moves aren't especially effective against Garchomp either, and Thunderbolt would just be absorbed by its Ground typing. I'm also considering that Garchomp likely outspeeds Gholdengo, which limits that plan's safety.

Still, Parting Shot seems like the stronger choice: it cuts Garchomp's Attack and Special Attack, softening its follow-up hits before Gholdengo takes the field. I'll go with Parting Shot.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is at 94 HP and will likely be hit hard by Earthquake again, since Ground is super effective on Fire/Dark. Opposing Mega Garchomp is at -2 Attack, so its Earthquake is weakened. My Garchomp is faster and takes only neutral Ground damage, and Outrage hits their Dragon/Ground Mega for 2x.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is at 94/202 after Earthquake, and with Garchomp's attack dropped two stages its offense is weaker now. Since switching is my only legal option, I'm weighing bringing in my own Garchomp, which should resist or be immune to Ground, versus switching to Gholdengo instead.

Actually my Garchomp takes Ground neutral rather than resisting it, while Gholdengo being Steel/Ghost is doubly weak to Ground, so Earthquake would hit it hard. I'm also comparing speed tiers between my Garchomp and the opposing Mega Garchomp to see who'd act first after the switch.

My Garchomp's Outrage would hit their Dragon/Ground Garchomp for 2x damage, and since their stats are already lowered from the previous Earthquake use, switching Garchomp in looks like the strong play. I'll go with switching to Garchomp, noting Earthquake doesn't trigger Rough Skin since it's not a contact move.

decisions.thought: Our Garchomp is faster than the opposing Mega Garchomp, and Outrage is super effective against it. Mega Evolving first gives us Sand Force and a stronger attack for no cost, while their Atk is at -2. Outrage should take most of their remaining HP.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
The opposing Mega Garchomp sits at 88% HP with its attack and special attack dropped, while our own Garchomp outspeeds it. I'm noting that Mega Evolving our Garchomp triggers Sand Force under the auto-sandstorm, which could boost our ground and rock moves if we go that route.

Outrage stands out as the best option since Dragon hits Garchomp's Dragon typing for double damage, and with 120 base power and STAB, Mega Garchomp's Outrage should knock off a huge chunk of the opponent's remaining health, likely 60-70%, far more effective than Earthquake which is only neutral against Garchomp's ground typing.

Comparing damage further: outrage with STAB and the double power against dragon type gives much higher output than earthquake even with the sand boost. Going with outrage while mega evolving.

decisions.thought: Only one legal action is available: Outrage. Mega Garchomp is faster than Archaludon, and Outrage is super effective on Steel/Dragon Archaludon, so it's the natural play.

Garchomp fainted, so I must switch. Gholdengo is at full HP with Life Orb and 203 base SpA, and Shadow Ball is neutral into Archaludon, which is already at 44%. Gholdengo should also outspeed or match Archaludon, making it the clear choice over the damaged Incineroar.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Garchomp down, I need to pick between Incineroar at 94/202 or full-health Gholdengo with Life Orb. Archaludon is at 44%, having boosted its Defense and dropped its own Special Attack, and since it's Steel/Dragon I'm weighing whether Gholdengo's Ghost or Steel-type moves can actually get through that defense boost.

Shadow Ball hits neutrally and should still deal solid damage with Gholdengo's 203 base Special Attack, likely securing the KO on Archaludon's remaining HP, while Gholdengo's speed also lets it act first. Incineroar at low HP risks going down to a Draco Meteor even with Archaludon's SpA drop, so Gholdengo is clearly the safer switch-in.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is at 44% and its Sp. Atk is at -2 after Draco Meteor, so it can't threaten Gholdengo much. Shadow Ball is neutral, and with Gholdengo's 203 Sp. Atk, Life Orb, and STAB it should knock out Archaludon. Thunderbolt and Make It Rain are resisted.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Archaludon is down to 44% HP after mega evolving, with its Defense boosted and Special Attack dropped from Draco Meteor. Gholdengo's Shadow Ball wouldn't be super effective here since Ghost is neutral against Steel/Dragon typing.

Checking Thunderbolt's effectiveness, Electric is neutral against Steel but resisted by Dragon, giving a 0.5x multiplier overall. Make It Rain faces a similar reduction since Steel resists Steel-type moves while Dragon is neutral to it.

Ball seems like the strongest option: Gholdengo's high Special Attack combined with STAB and Life Orb should deal heavy damage to Archaludon regardless of its Special Defense investment, likely securing a KO, especially since Archaludon's offensive stats take a hit if it's Mega Evolved.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo outspeeds Mega Incineroar, and Thunderbolt is neutral against Fire/Dark with 203 Sp. Atk plus Life Orb, so it should deal the most damage. Make It Rain is resisted by Fire, and Shadow Ball is resisted by Dark. Nasty Plot lets Incineroar hit hard first.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Against Mega Incineroar's Fire/Dark typing, Shadow Ball is resisted by Dark, but Thunderbolt hits neutrally, so I'm leaning toward Thunderbolt as the better coverage option here.

Make It Rain is halved by Fire resistance despite neutral Dark, so that's weaker here. Meanwhile Mega Incineroar's own Flare Blitz and Darkest Lariat both hit Gholdengo super effectively, so I should prioritize maximizing immediate damage with Thunderbolt rather than setting up with Nasty Plot.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo has fainted, so the only legal action is switching in Incineroar at 46.5% HP. I have to pick that single option.

Our Incineroar is slower than or close to the opposing Mega Incineroar, but Fake Out has +3 priority, so it moves first. It deals roughly 27 damage, which doesn't KO, but the flinch stops their Flare Blitz this turn. Next turn Flare Blitz should finish the target.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking HP totals: our Incineroar at 94/202, opponent's Mega Incineroar around 31%. I'm puzzling over whether Fake Out is actually usable here since Incineroar's been on the field since turn 6, but the move is still showing as legal, so maybe the restriction works differently than I assumed.

Fake Out would deal roughly 27 damage, not enough to KO since it lacks STAB. Flare Blitz hits harder, around 50-55 damage after resistance, putting the opponent near a coin-flip KO range, but the recoil is risky given our own HP is already low. I'm also noting that our Intimidate should have dropped the opponent's Attack stage already.

Weighing speed, I'm uncertain whether we outpace their Incineroar since its Speed range could be anywhere from 72 to 123, and Fake Out always moves first regardless. If I don't get a Fake Out flinch to set up a clean follow-up, Protect or Parting Shot might be safer options, though switching out is complicated since I don't know what's left on our bench. Flare Blitz for the potential KO seems like the strongest play if we can confirm we move first.

decisions.thought: The opposing Mega Incineroar has only about 16% HP, roughly 32 HP. Even though Flare Blitz is not very effective, our Incineroar's 183 Attack should still deal around 55 damage, which is enough to knock it out. Our Incineroar is slightly faster on base speed, so Flare Blitz is the best play.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking matchup details: our Incineroar is at 94/202 HP while the opponent's Mega Incineroar is down to about 16%, still affected by our Intimidate drop. I'm weighing whether Flare Blitz would even be effective against their Fire/Dark typing.

Running the damage math, our Flare Blitz should still knock out the opponent despite resisted Fire-on-Fire damage, since they're already so low. The bigger question is speed and turn order—if they go first with their own Flare Blitz, they could threaten to KO us too, so I'm weighing whether Protect is the safer play here, factoring in the recoil cost of Flare Blitz either way.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is faster and can likely KO our 47 HP Incineroar before Flare Blitz resolves, so attacking now is a gamble. Protect blocks its move, and Dracometeor's self-drop weakens its follow-up. Next turn, Flare Blitz can finish it if it stays in.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar at low HP against the faster Mega Archaludon, I'm checking Flare Blitz's effectiveness — since Archaludon is Steel/Dragon, Fire hits Steel for 2x but Dragon resists at 0.5x, netting out to neutral damage.

Calculating the numbers, Flare Blitz should still easily knock out Archaludon even with its boosted Mega defenses. But since Archaludon is faster, it could hit first with Draco Meteor and kill Incineroar before it even attacks, making Protect a tempting option to consider.

Even accounting for Dracometeor's self-lowering SpA, a second hit next turn would still likely finish Incineroar off since it moves first. Realistically, Flare Blitz is the only move that actually threatens damage here, even if it's risky; Parting Shot doesn't save much since Incineroar's at 47 HP and dies to nearly any hit regardless, so swapping it out just to preserve momentum might be the safer play.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is faster and its Draco Meteor will likely KO my 47 HP Incineroar before Flare Blitz resolves, and Flare Blitz is resisted anyway. Protect has +4 priority, so it blocks the Draco Meteor this turn and keeps Incineroar alive.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar at 47 HP and Archaludon mega outspeeding, Draco Meteor is likely lethal before I can act, so I'm weighing whether Flare Blitz actually gets through given fire's super-effective hit on steel despite dragon's partial resistance.

Protect would stop this turn's attack but doesn't fix the speed problem next turn. Parting Shot could debuff and swap out, but with Gholdengo already down I'm not sure I have a bench mon left to switch into, so the move might just fail or leave me stuck.

Since Archaludon likely outspeeds and Draco Meteor would knock out Incineroar before Flare Blitz connects anyway, Protect is the safer choice here to avoid losing the mon for free this turn.
